newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Littlewoods buy ups threat to GUS.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Littlewoods buy ups threat to GUS.

text.p: Britain's Littlewoods Organisation said on Monday its acquisition of Freemans agency mail order business would boost its ability to compete with Great Universal Stores Plc in the home shopping market.

Littlewoods chairman James Ross said the privately-owned retailer's acquisition of Freemans from Sears Plc would raise its share of Britain's home shopping market by some eight percent to roughly 26 percent, compared to GUS' 29 percent.
"If we put our business and Sears' together, then we will be very close to the market leader, GUS, and that gives us lots of opportunities to be very competitive," Ross told Reuters.
He added that the company decided to make the 395 million stg acquisition partly as a result of consolidations in the declining agency mail order sector.

"If you want to have a profitable role in a consolidating industry, then you need to be a very major player. Otherwise you might as well get out, which is presumably what Sears felt about Freemans," Ross said.
The acquisition could increase Littlewoods Home Shopping Group's contribution to group trading profits to about 70-75 percent in two or three years from the current level of 50-60 percent, he said.
Combined annual turnover for the home shopping businesses would be about 1.5 billion stg.
Ross said financing costs for the acquisition would put pressure on earnings initially.
"Very short term, it will be dilutive, and then it will be positive," he said, adding that the company would probably take write-offs to goodwill for the acquisition.
Ross said the firm planned to continue growing its home shopping business and was looking at selling goods directly to consumers via cable television.
"I think we'll get into it, the question is how. It may often pay you to be an informed follower, and someone else can be the first to make the mistakes," he said.
Regarding other businesses, Ross said the company currently planned to retain its Littlewoods Stores chain, despite the unit's disappointing trading profits.

"The current plan is to manage it tightly and make it effective while we're re-examining the long-term future of the stores, and that will take a few weeks or months," he said, adding that the company had halted expansion plans at the chain.
Littlewoods Stores like-for-like sales rose 3.4 percent in the six weeks to December 28 compared to the year-ago period.
